content: Possible side effects of this medication include headaches, as well as burning, itching, or pain in the vaginal or urethral area. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of potential side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you experience any side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the United States, you can also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088. In Canada, you can report side effects to Health Canada. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungal agents (such as clotrimazole or fluconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Consult your doctor to determine whether it is safe to engage in sexual intercourse while using this product. Be aware that this medication may weaken rubber products such as latex condoms, diaphragms, or cervical caps, potentially leading to failure and an increased risk of pregnancy. Avoid using these products during treatment and for three days after completing treatment. Do not use this medication for self-treatment if you are pregnant. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, and you should follow your doctor’s instructions on how to use the applicator to insert the medication. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. If someone has overdosed on this medication and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call the Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222. To help prevent vaginal yeast infections, thoroughly dry the genital area after showering, bathing, or swimming. Avoid wearing tight jeans, nylon underwear, pantyhose, wet bathing suits, or damp/sweaty exercise clothes for extended periods. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. For further guidance, consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
